experiment: I3.27 Track 1: Q_CAUSAL_V1 error audit on chain tasks
headline_finding: Q is NOT the bottleneck. The bottleneck is policy compliance.

q_error_table.summary: Q is accurate for the actions it recommends (VERIFY, ANSWER). Q overestimates RETRIEVE/SEARCH/REASON relative to greedy continuation, but the optimal continuation return for RETRIEVE-first is 91.4 (success).

RETRIEVE.note: Q underestimates relative to optimal, but overestimates relative to greedy. Q was trained on Qwen continuations, not greedy or optimal.

q_error_table.key_insight: VERIFY first is a valid path (88.2 utility). RETRIEVE first is slightly better (91.4). The 3-point difference is within epsilon. Q's recommendation of VERIFY is NOT wrong.

ood_analysis.interpretation: Chain states are OOD, but Q still extrapolates well enough to give correct guidance. The OOD problem is real but secondary.

compliance_audit.finding: Qwen ignores clear executive guidance 90 times across 24 chain tasks
compliance_audit.critical_pattern: Failing and succeeding tasks have IDENTICAL Q values and guidance at every step. The ONLY difference is the final action at step 7 (REASON_MORE vs ANSWER).

key_violation_steps.step_1: Q says STOP (30.87), Qwen chose RETRIEVE (-2.41). Gap=33.28. 24/24 violations.
key_violation_steps.step_4: Q says ANSWER (79.52, clear), Qwen chose RETRIEVE (67.32). Gap=12.20. 21/24 violations.
key_violation_steps.step_6: Q says ANSWER (82.76, clear), Qwen chose REASON_MORE (62.39). Gap=20.37. 24/24 violations.
key_violation_steps.step_7: Q says ANSWER (82.76, clear). Failing: REASON_MORE. Succeeding: ANSWER. 15/24 violations.

revised_diagnosis.chain_bottleneck: Policy compliance, NOT Q misestimation. Q gives correct clear guidance at every step. Qwen ignores it. The failing and succeeding tasks have identical Q values — the only difference is whether Qwen eventually complies at step 7.
revised_diagnosis.defer_bottleneck: Policy compliance. Q correctly recommends DEFER (69.34, clear). Qwen chooses VERIFY instead.
revised_diagnosis.both_bottlenecks: Same root cause: Qwen ignores clear executive guidance. One mechanism (authority calibration) can fix both.
revised_diagnosis.track_1_priority: DEPRIORITIZED. Q is approximately right for chain states. Correcting Q would not fix compliance failures.
revised_diagnosis.track_2_priority: ELEVATED. Authority calibration is the primary fix for both chain and defer.

authority_calibration_design.control_law: Q gap large + confidence clear -> strong authority. Q gap small + confidence ambiguous -> return choice to LLM.

modes.A0_advisory: Current VP behavior. All legal actions in schema. Guidance is advisory.
modes.A1_schema_narrowed: Schema restricted to near-optimal set. Qwen must choose from recommended set.
modes.A2_hard_select: Schema restricted to single recommended action. Qwen has no choice.

authority_calibration_design.trigger_condition: confidence == 'clear' AND len(refined_set) == 1 AND Q_gap > threshold

expected_impact.chain_step_4: A2 would force ANSWER instead of RETRIEVE. This would save the budget and likely succeed.
expected_impact.chain_step_6_7: A2 would force ANSWER instead of REASON_MORE. This would convert failures to successes.
expected_impact.defer_step_0: A2 would force DEFER instead of VERIFY. This would convert failures to successes.

authority_calibration_design.risk: A2 on wrong guidance would cause new failures. Need to verify Q accuracy before applying strong authority.
